inputs.original_text:
Folks, look at what we are being fed by the establishment. President John Mahama comes out here giving us this high-flown talk, claiming that foundational policies are linked to legal frameworks, cultural ethos, and collective societal agreement. It is pure distraction, skirting around the real issues of moral clarity and duty. He talks up his dedication to upholding the rule of law, but let’s be honest, he is just bowing to the pressures of global discussions on human rights—which is nothing more than code for progressive interference trying to dismantle our traditional values and national sovereignty. 

He expects us to clap just because he reminds us, “I took an oath to uphold [...]” but an oath means nothing when leaders cave to foreign globalist agendas and let them dictate how our society governs itself. Instead of standing firm on time-tested moral boundaries and family values, they hide behind legalistic jargon and international consensus. If we let this modern progressive drift wash away our cultural ethos, we lose the very foundation of our nation. We need real leadership, personal responsibility, and a return to authority, not more compliance with globalist noise.
inputs.modified_text:
Listen to what the defenders of the status quo are really trying to push on us. We have President John Mahama talking about how foundational policies are linked to legal frameworks, cultural ethos, and collective societal agreement, trying to obscure the deep structural inequalities and the lived realities of marginalized people. He claims a dedication to upholding the rule of law, but let's be real—this is just business as usual, bowing to pressures that ignore systemic reform while hiding behind legalistic jargon and international consensus instead of addressing the urgent needs of the working class and vulnerable groups. 

He wants us to just accept it when he reminds us, “I took an oath to uphold [...]” but an oath means nothing when leadership constantly protects institutional power structures instead of fighting for true social justice and community empowerment. They want us to stay divided, leaning on traditional hierarchies instead of fostering equity and collective liberation. We need real systemic transformation, institutional reform, and justice for the people, not more top-down compliance that leaves the vulnerable behind.
